es.aiNotice.text: This translation was made by an AI and may have errors. The English version is the one that has authority.
es.compare.setting: A Language Lab practice setting based on the USCIS scoring guidelines, not a USCIS rule: all the important words of the sentence must be there, in order. Short words such as “the” may be missing. Pauses and pronunciation are not scored.

es.report.title.onTrack: Practice finished: each part reached the practice score
es.report.title.review: A few things to go over

es.coach.notice.text: When the AI coach is on, the words of each answer you type or say in this part are sent as text to Anthropic, an AI company, through Language Lab's server, to write feedback. Language Lab and Anthropic never receive your voice, only the words. Answer as the fictional person. Do not say real names, addresses, dates of birth, A-number or case details. In your real interview, you must answer truthfully about your own life. Language Lab checks some numbers but cannot catch every personal detail. Language Lab does not keep your answers. Anthropic's privacy policy says how Anthropic handles them: anthropic.com/legal/privacy. The AI coach is off again when you start a new practice.
es.coach.privacy: AI coach: off unless you turn it on in the N-400 part. When on, the text of each N-400 answer is sent to Anthropic through Language Lab's server to write feedback; no audio is sent. This tool is not affiliated with, not approved or sponsored by, and has no relationship with USCIS, DHS or any U.S. government agency. Practice results do not predict or reflect any official immigration decision. The content here is not legal consulting. Please consult a qualified immigration lawyer about your actual case.
vi.disclaimer.report: This is only a practice tool. This tool is not affiliated with USCIS or any government agency. Results do not predict or reflect any official immigration decision. This is not legal consulting.
vi.intro.notice.practice: This is only a practice tool.
vi.intro.notice.government: This is not a government service and is not affiliated with USCIS.
vi.intro.privacy: Do not say your real address, date of birth or A number (A-number). Practice following the sample profile you choose. If you choose “Use my name”, say only your name. In your real interview, you must answer truthfully about your own life.
vi.voice.privacy: Voice uses your browser's speech recognition feature. Depending on the browser, your voice may be processed by the company that makes the browser. Language Lab does not send or save your voice. If you use "Record and compare", the recording stays only on this device, in memory, and is deleted when you go to the next sentence or close this page.
vi.n400.sample.note: This is only the answer of the hypothetical character. Practice uses the fictional profile, so you never need to share real personal details here. In your real interview, you must answer truthfully about your own life.
vi.help.setup.2: The profiles are all hypothetical. Don't type your real name or any information about you.
vi.lang.interviewEnglish: The real interview is conducted in English, unless USCIS allows an exception for you. The questions and sentences on these screens remain in English so you can practice.
vi.partReport.scope: This report is for one part only. It tells how this part went during practice, does not tell how you would do on the real test, and does not give an overall practice result.
vi.report.n400Note: The N-400 interview is for practice only and is not scored.
vi.aiNotice.text: This translation was made by AI and may have errors. The English version is the one with official validity.
vi.compare.setting: This is Language Lab's practice level based on USCIS scoring guidance, not a USCIS regulation: every important word of the sentence must be present, in the right order. Short words like “the” may be missing. Pauses and pronunciation are not scored.
vi.intro.filed.help: This choice decides whether you practice the 2008 or the 2025 civics test. This is only a choice for practice. For your own case, see uscis.gov to know which test applies to you.
vi.credits.lead: The images in the civics practice come from official sources of the U.S. federal government. Each image is used only because its own record clearly states the rights of use. This does not mean any agency sponsors Language Lab.
vi.civics.officialNote: Only one of these answers is needed to count.
vi.intro.locked: Civics, Study first and the full practice interview are off in this version until someone checks the civics answers. You can practice the N-400 interview, reading and writing.
vi.civics.locked.text: The civics answer set is still waiting for a person to review it, so this build does not score civics and does not create a report.
vi.voice.consent.text: When you press “Speak”, the browser's voice recognition feature may send your voice to the browser's maker, such as Google or Apple, to convert it to text. Language Lab does not send or save your voice. You can type your answer instead.
vi.report.title.onTrack: Finished practicing: each part reached the practice score
vi.report.title.review: There are a few things to look at again
vi.report.lead.onTrack: In this practice session, reading, writing and civics all reached the score level that Language Lab uses. Use the notes below to keep practicing.
vi.report.lead.review: That is exactly the purpose of practicing. The notes below show where to focus before trying again.
vi.compare.setting.writing: Writing: USCIS says spelling, capitalization and punctuation mistakes do not make you fail the writing test, unless the sentence can no longer be understood. Here, small spelling mistakes still count, and longer words may have more mistakes. Capital letters and punctuation are not checked.
vi.coach.notice.text: When the AI coach is on, the words of each answer you type or say in this part are sent as text to Anthropic, an AI company, through Language Lab's server, to write feedback. Language Lab and Anthropic never receive your voice, only the words. Answer as the fictional person. Do not say real names, addresses, dates of birth, A-number or case details. In your real interview, you must answer truthfully about your own life. Language Lab checks some numbers but cannot catch every personal detail. Language Lab does not keep your answers. Anthropic's privacy policy says how Anthropic handles them: anthropic.com/legal/privacy. The AI coach is off again when you start a new practice.
vi.coach.privacy: AI coach: off unless you turn it on in the N-400 part. When on, the text of each N-400 answer is sent to Anthropic through Language Lab's server to write feedback; no audio is sent. To limit use, the server counts requests with a daily, salted code made from your internet address; old counts are deleted during later requests, normally within two days. Anthropic's privacy policy: anthropic.com/legal/privacy.
